EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.Method.Name: Penalty Assignment
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.Method.Hint: Method A fills the Extended Exhaustion table left to right, completing each row before moving to the next. Method B lets each player distribute their own levels across the six penalty types.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.MaxLevel.Hi: The highest survivable level of exhaustion, in multiples of the six penalty columns. A creature dies one level past this. The speed and hit point maximum penalties scale from it. Requires a reload.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.RecoveryBas: Long rest recovery saves use a DC of this value minus the creature's current exhaustion level.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.LongRestRec: On completing a long rest, remove one level of exhaustion and then roll the escalating Constitution saving throws automatically.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.ZeroHPExhau: Automatically apply one level of exhaustion when a creature drops to 0 hit points.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.MinimumRoll: Enforce the rule that exhaustion cannot reduce an ability check or saving throw below 1.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.MinimumSpee: Enforce the rule that a speed reduced to 0 feet or less by exhaustion becomes 1 foot instead.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.ApplySpeedT: Apply the speed penalty to every movement type the creature has, matching how the dnd5e system handles exhaustion. Disable to reduce only walking speed.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.EnableSpend: Let creatures voluntarily gain exhaustion to fuel desperate actions and magical power.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Settings.SheetTracke: Replace the dnd5e exhaustion pips with a badge that opens the Extended Exhaustion tracker.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.mentalSkills.H: Intelligence-, Wisdom- and Charisma-based ability checks
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.physicalSkills: Strength-, Dexterity- and Constitution-based ability checks
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.mentalSaves.Hi: Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws
Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.speed.Label: Speed
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.speed.Hint: Movement speed, to a minimum of 1 foot
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.hpMax.Label: Hit Point Maximum
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Track.hpMax.Hint: Hit point maximum, to a minimum of 1
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Reason.Travel: Travelled more than 8 hours in a day
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Reason.Effect: Suffered an effect that causes exhaustion
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.Name: Extended Exhaustion {level}
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.Description: Cumulative penalties from the Extended Exhaustion table. Speed and hit point maximum penalties are applied directly to derived data and so are not listed as changes here.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.Failed: The mechanical effect could not be applied; apply it manually.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.SlotGranted: A level {level} spell slot was added to the sheet.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.Healed: Regained {amount} hit points, one {denominator}th of the maximum.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.NoSlotLevel: This creature has no level {level} spell slots to add to.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.NoFeature: No feature with limited uses matching "{name}" was found.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.FeatureFull: {name} already has all of its uses available.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.AdvantageGran: Advantage on attack rolls until the end of this turn.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.CritDieGrante: One extra melee critical damage die until the end of this turn.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.MovedToTop: Moved to the top of the initiative order.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.NotInCombat: Not in combat, so there is no initiative order to move within.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.DeathSaveRero: The failed death saving throw was taken back and rerolled.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.DeathSaveCanc: The reroll was cancelled, so nothing was changed.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Effect.NoFailedDeath: There is no failed death saving throw to reroll.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Notification.Unconsc: An unconscious creature cannot voluntarily spend exhaustion, except to reroll a death saving throw.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Notification.Lethal: Spending {cost} would push exhaustion past {max} from its current level of {level}, which would be fatal.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Tracker.Title: Extended Exhaustion
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Tracker.Dead: This creature's exhaustion level is fatal.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Tracker.ChoiceHint: Method B: distribute levels across the six penalty types however you like. Changes apply as you make them.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Tracker.SequentialHi: Method A: the table fills left to right, one row at a time. Changes apply as you make them.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Tracker.Scale: Table is {rows} rows deep: each column holds at most {rows} marks, worth -{speed} ft. of speed and -1/{zeroAt} hit points each.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Place.Prompt: Choose which penalty this level of exhaustion is marked against.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Place.Title: Place Exhaustion
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Place.PromptMany: Choose where each level is marked — {remaining} of {count} still to place.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Place.AutoPlaced: No column was chosen, so {name}'s new level of exhaustion was placed automatically. Open the exhaustion tracker to move it.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Card.Dead: Exhaustion has reached a fatal level.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Recovery.Title: Long Rest Recovery
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Recovery.Subtitle: Remove one level, then save until you fail
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Recovery.Automatic: One level removed at the end of the long rest.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Recovery.Deprived: No exhaustion is recovered while starving or parched.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.Intro: Exhaustion represents a creature pushing itself beyond its normal limits. Spend it to fuel desperate actions or magical power.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.Disabled: Spending exhaustion is disabled in this world.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.BeyondMax: Beyond my highest slot level (double cost)
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.UnconsciousNot: This creature is unconscious, so only the death save reroll is available.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.Blocked.Lethal: Not enough room before a fatal exhaustion level.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.spellSlot1.Des: If you have no spell slots remaining, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to cast a 1st-level spell.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.healing.Label: Catch Your Breath
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.healing.Descri: You can gain 1 level of exhaustion to regain hit points equal to one {denominator}th of your hit point maximum, to a minimum of 1. You cannot use this option at 0 hit points.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.upcast.Label: Upcast
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.upcast.Descrip: You can gain 1 level of exhaustion per spell level to cast a spell at a higher level. If you cast a spell beyond the highest level of spell slot normally available to you, the cost is 2 levels of exhaustion per spell level.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.upcast.BeyondM: , beyond the highest slot level normally available
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.extraAttack.De: When you take the Attack action, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to make one additional weapon attack as part of that action.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.rage.Label: Rage
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.rage.Descripti: If you have no uses of Rage remaining, you can gain 2 levels of exhaustion to enter your Rage.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.recklessAttack: When you make melee weapon attacks during your turn, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to gain advantage on all of those attack rolls, rather than only the first attack roll made using Reckless Attack.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.brutalCritical: When you score a critical hit, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to roll one additional weapon damage die as part of the critical hit.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.kiPoints.Label: Ki Points
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.kiPoints.Descr: If you have no ki points remaining, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to recover 2 ki points. If you shout "Kaioken!" when using this feature, you instead recover 3 ki points.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.negateCritical: When you would take a critical hit, you can use your reaction and gain 1 level of exhaustion to turn the critical hit into a normal hit.
You can gain 1 level of exhaustion to take an additional reaction before the start of your next turn. You can take only one reaction per trigger.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.crucialSave.De: When you make a saving throw, you can gain 1 level of exhaustion to add a +5 bonus to the roll. You can use this option after rolling the d20, but before the DM determines whether the roll succeeds or fails.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.crucialSave.Ap: The +5 bonus was added to the most recent saving throw.
You can gain 1 level of exhaustion to act immediately, regardless of your position in the initiative order. This does not grant you an additional turn. Instead, you move to the top of the initiative order and act normally on this turn and all subsequent turns.
EXTENDED_EXHAUSTION.Spend.rerollDeathSav: When you fail a death saving throw, you can use your reaction and gain 2 levels of exhaustion to reroll the saving throw. You must use the new result.
